key: v6.7 (2 Nov) — Fable's data pass on chapter one, from the game's copy. Settings: 14 placeholders checked; graphQuestionGapShare 0.10 → 0.15; legRounding added (legs round up to the quarter hour); homeTurnaroundMin 35 → 30; rivalTakeover note added · Routes colour: 18 checked against BertieV4's role colours. Amsterdam #c0703a → #a8714f and Barcelona #a8874f → #9c8a62 (the originals read as amber and gold, which mean warning and money); the other 16 kept · Wording: '£3.00 a litre' → '£2.94'; stray 'snacks' removed from Launch Day text; December's fuel line and the end's 'reputation revealed' corrected (2 cells) · ScreenText: 84 placeholders checked. rival.week and board.note retired (no longer shown); 'shareholders' → 'the airline's owners' on the Board's card; 'fly {city}' → 'fly to {city}'; the graph question's answer line now says what it is (best plan − yours); 'Here's a simpler way' → 'A quicker way'; launch.compare flagged against D109. Decisions left to Bertie (rules, not figures): the two Boards; whether Red Kite takes only routes he had time to fly; a cap on the graph question; the strength of the fare swing; week-1 Day pages. See Fable-Data-Pass-Report-2-Nov.md.

Fable, 2 Nov: this is the 'Red Kite takes over an unflown route' mechanic Bertie asked for on 2 Nov. It is separate from the Red Kite undercut event, which stays parked (rivalUndercut off).

new: Fable, 2 Nov: 35 → 30 (a Twin Otter turnaround). With legs rounded to the quarter, two Frankfurt flights and one Paris take 12 h 00 and fit the 12-hour duty day; Dublin ×2 + Paris ×2 take 11 h 30.
